argv:
Rewrite the text as a stage pirate would tell it.

Use "ye" for "you", "be" for "is" and "are", and "aye" for "yes". Use nautical
vocabulary: crew, deck, helm, cargo, port, tide, chart. Address the reader as
a shipmate. Add "arr" sparingly, at most once per paragraph.

Keep every fact of the original. Do not add a plot, a ship, or characters that
were not in the source.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
The Millbrook Hollow City Council voted Tuesday night to approve an amended version of the parks and recreation line item, following a meeting that also touched on the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge. According to a spokesperson for the mayor's office, the revised figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members, though the spokesperson declined to characterize those conversations further. A separate memo, attributed by two council staffers to the finance subcommittee, put the adjustment at approximately $340,000, a figure that a budget analyst who reviewed the memo said was "in the range we expected." Buried near the end of that same memo, and not raised by any council member during the meeting, was a line noting that the bridge's lead structural engineer had flagged a load-bearing crack serious enough to warrant closing the span to truck traffic within 90 days. The bridge project, which has appeared on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has already drawn 14 change orders, was not discussed in detail. Council member Dana Okafor, reached after the meeting, said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
</passage>

response.text:
Ahoy, shipmate, gather round and hear the tale from the Millbrook Hollow council deck. On Tuesday eve, the council crew voted aye to approve an amended parks and recreation line item, and the meetin' also touched upon the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge. A spokesperson for the mayor's office says the revised figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among the crew of council members, though she wouldn't chart out those conversations any further, arr.

A separate memo, credited by two council staffers to the finance subcommittee, put the adjustment at near $340,000 — a sum a budget analyst who reviewed the memo called "in the range we expected." But buried near the end o' that same memo, and never raised by a single council member durin' the meetin', was a line notin' that the bridge's lead structural engineer had flagged a load-bearin' crack serious enough to close the span to truck traffic within 90 days' tide.

The bridge project, sittin' on the capital plan's chart since at least 2019 and already draggin' 14 change orders behind it like barnacles on the hull, weren't discussed in any detail. Council member Dana Okafor, reached after the meetin', said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
